authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11503.1 vātiṅgaṇa gives Punjabi/Hindi baigan and Bengali begun “eggplant”. It separately lists Bastar bāṅgā in 11503.5 vaṅga; the survey banga form selects that contracted branch, not the full head. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8376.1 *peṭṭa gives Hindi/Bengali peṭ and Oriya peṭa “belly”, distinct from poṭṭa and peḍḍuka. The survey pet spellings preserve the diagnostic e-vowel belly family, with the source’s dental-versus-retroflex transcription retained for audit rather than silently normalized in the data. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 4368 grāma explicitly gives Lahnda/Punjabi girā̃/grā̃ and eastern gā̃/gām, with learned gram readily identifiable. It also lists a -ṭa extension in gāmaḍa; unexplained survey gauḍa/gāvḍo contraction needs a local account. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

It explicitly separates Torwali/Maiya duāš under 6658.2 duvādaśa; those survey forms are assigned to the latter node. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.
